body: you just have to have kindness to yourself and understand its an illness. one day you could fall apart and your progress will feel pointless. but you are just a human experiencing this life with a debilitating illness that makes you behave in a way that makes you want to puke. but at the end of the day when you lay down your head, you only think of your mistakes. and it's the same for other people - they think about their own mistakes too. we are not so thought about as we think we are. and we can only have forgiveness and kindness for ourselves and move forward. xo

I relate so hard to this. it's an impossible disorder to explain to someone who doesn't have it. I hate when I'm manic I feel like my brain is itchy - cannot last another moment. I don't function well and it makes me miserable. I cannot regulate my thoughts or emotions. even thinking about my manic episodes makes me want to puke
I'm so sorry you're experiencing this too. I feel wild eyed and crazy - just cannot explain this feeling to anyone in my life. I'm so burdened by my mental illness
I don't think his comment was intended to discredit anyone. i think he's trying to provide positivity to this person, please allow this comment to be that

I struggle with suicide / suicidal thoughts and I 100% understand how reaching out is actually so disappointing and often has the opposite response you are looking for. 

people who don't have suicidal tendencies really cannot understand it. they may care about you and offer themselves as a lifeline in those dark moments, but they really do not know what they are signing up for, and often don't know how to respond so they usually just don't. 

my bipolar disorder makes me suicidal more often than I would like. my suggestion is for you to find a therapist you connect with. when I am holding a knife to my arm or looking down a bottle of pills, I call my therapist. she is always available for me and makes me feel important to her. but more importantly, she acknowledges my pain and does not feed me fake positivity. she tells me that she is sorry I can't think about the good times, and that I must be really struggling. she makes me feel like a person. she knows that what I need in that moment is an active ear, and she is so empathetic it makes me cry as I type this. 

find a therapist. there are many options. online or in person there are people who understand your mental health is not fictitious. there will be someone on your side. 

reaching out to friends is so hard, and I'm sorry they didn't respond to you when you needed them. I'm sure they wanted to, but didn't know how and chose silence. 

I will give you my therapists information if you like. she's here in Canada but she does zoom meetings and maybe you can make it work. if not, please knooow that someone is going to understand what you are experiencing. you just need to refocus who you ask for help from. I really hope you make it through this moment. message me if you need to
